distributor.name: City of Ekurhuleni Energy Department
distributor.notes: 2026/27 Schedule 2 of Electricity Tariffs (1 Jul 2026 - 30 Jun 2027) states all tariffs EXCLUDE VAT. Major structural changes for 2026/27: residential inclining block tariff abolished in favour of a flat rate above 50 kWh.

approved_increase.notes: City press release and IOL (2 July 2026): electricity +8.76% 'in line with tariff guidelines approved by NERSA'; city flyer: average across ALL tariffs 9.01%, Municflex-linked Tariffs I/J/G +8.76%. CONFLICT (documented, recheck 2026-07-05): The Citizen/CCE roundups report 12.7% as Ekurhuleni's NERSA-approved increase, and Moneyweb reports the NERSA-approved application is under legal challenge — industrial users allege a >R7bn miscalculation of Eskom bulk purchases plus a further R6.6bn in errors, questioning the tariffs' legality. Most plausible reading: 12.7% is the NERSA-approved application figure (contested), while 8.76%/9.01% are the guideline-linked figures the city publicly communicated and implemented in its Schedule 2. Not yet numerically reconciled by any source.

tariff_plans.name: Tariff A.2 — Residential non-indigent (conventional and prepaid incl. IMMS)
tariff_plans.notes: Converted from inclining block tariff to a single flat rate for all units above 50 kWh; no basic charge linked to this tariff. Schedule splits A.2.1 High Demand Season (Jun-Aug) and A.2.2 Low Demand Season (Sep-May). An unverified search summary quoted R3.0635/kWh for both seasons — excluded pending confirmation. 2025/26 comparators (NOT 2026/27): IBT R3.25 (0-600), R5.08 (600-700), R13.16 (>700). Recheck 2026-07-05: draft Schedule 2 indexed text contains values R3.7971 and R2.4874 per kWh WITHOUT visible tariff-category context — not mapped to any component; R3.0635 remains neither confirmed nor refuted.
